hourly.summary: Arsenal dropped two points in a 2-2 draw at St James' Park after a dominant first half collapsed into chaos, and the post-match mood is dominated by genuine dread over David Raya's shoulder injury — 'could kill this team' was the recurring refrain. Fans are questioning the midfield balance with Bruno Guimarães running the show for Newcastle, debating whether Saliba returns to shore up the defence, and eyeing the title gap nervously as Liverpool loom. There's also background noise about Ødegaard and Havertz contract talks stalling, but the Raya situation has sucked all the oxygen out of the room.

daily.summary: The day began in brutal despair (3/10) after Arsenal Women's heavy Champions League defeat to Lyon dominated early discourse, with fans calling for the manager's dismissal. Sentiment gradually improved to concerned (5/10) as attention split between the women's struggles and men's injury/transfer anxieties, before settling at cautious optimism (7/10) by evening as the men's team topped the table with Saliba returning for a sixth straight win chase — though typical neuroses around signings and injuries persisted.

weekly.summary: Arsenal fan sentiment traced a dramatic upward arc across the week, shifting from early anxiety over transfers, refereeing, and injury fears (5/10) through a measured, resilient midweek phase to a late-week surge of unity and triumph. The turning point arrived with collective solidarity for Arseblog's Andrew Mangan, followed by contract optimism and youth breakthroughs, culminating in euphoric delirium as Arsenal players starred in England's World Cup final victory. The week exemplifies the fanbase's volatility — oscillating between neuroses and peak joy — but finishes on a definitive high.\n
